$comment: Operations of the API that no SDK's hand-written layer models, and why. `scripts/sdk-contract/build.py --check` fails on an operation that is neither claimed by a manifest nor matched here, and on an entry here that matches nothing the API still serves. So this file is the record of a decision, not a place to make a failure go away: a new endpoint stops CI until somebody either wires it into a client or writes one line about why no client needs it. Patterns are fnmatch globs over `METHOD /path`, with the path exactly as the OpenAPI document templates it.

omit.reason: Account bootstrap. These sign-in and account recovery flows belong to the console and to `fountain auth login` (#1305). FountainKit models API key management after authentication.

Claimable principal lifecycle and owner-authenticated credential management (ADRs 0044 and 0053). Applications open grants with their full-scope key; visitors claim with their own account key. The principal credential then uses the modeled resource API. Current-owner inference credential PUT/DELETE operations also use plain HTTP; principal-scoped keys cannot call them.

Self-service OAuth client registration (#1125, ADR 0021). A person registers an app once, in the console or with `fountain oauth-client`, and then puts the returned client_id in the app. An SDK caller's work starts after that point, with the API key the flow mints, and every endpoint a client then calls is already modelled.
Sign in with Fountain. The browser apps exchange the code+PKCE themselves; the SDK starts with the API key that flow mints. FountainKit models revocation for sign-out.
Account self-service: billing, credit checkout, data exports, inference credentials, onboarding. The console owns all of it and none of it is part of running an agent.
Webhook registration and delivery replay. Server-to-server configuration a person does once in the console; nothing an SDK caller does per run.

The opt-in asynchronous start lifecycle (ADR 0042). Every SDK's run handle promises an immediate conversation, while a queued start first hands back a sandbox request; callers can reach these three over the raw HTTP client until a queued-run handle owns the polling and the cancellation without weakening that promise.
Egress broker bindings (ADR 0019). Configuration of where a credential lives, set once per account; the run-time effect is invisible to a client.
The self-hosted runner daemon's WebSocket (ADR 0022). Its socket is not JSON over HTTP. FountainKit models runner listing and deletion.
The Buzz gateway's own provisioning surface (ADR 0020). Buzz calls it; no general client does.
The AG-UI event stream. A second wire dialect for the same turn, consumed by AG-UI clients that already have their own protocol library; the SDKs follow /events and /stream instead.
The OpenAI-compatible gateway. Its clients are OpenAI SDKs by definition — that is the whole point of the shape.
The support inbox and report submission. No SDK models this console surface; FountainKit models the tenant's audit trail separately.
Avatar upload and generation belong to the console. FountainKit models fetching the image bytes.
Console-facing reads. No SDK models these operations. FountainKit separately models connection providers and turn images.
kubelet's probes. Unauthenticated, and about the deployment rather than the API.
PUT aliases of the PATCH routes, kept for clients that only speak PUT. The SDKs model the PATCH, and the two share a controller action.
